title: AWS CWI Exam Prep Course: 6-Day CWI Training
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep: Parts A, B and C, code book practice, eligibility and the vision test. Study online or train your team on site. Request a quote.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep Course: Six Days to Prepare for the Certified Welding Inspector Exam
html:
The AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) credential is the welding inspection qualification that US fabrication contracts, structural steel specifications and pipeline construction jobs ask for by name. Atlantis NDT runs a six-day (6-day) exam-preparation course for welders, fitters, QC staff, NDT technicians and engineers who plan to sit the AWS CWI examination. The course covers all three parts of the exam, Fundamentals, Practical and Code Application, with original practice questions and timed mock papers. The American Welding Society (AWS) administers the CWI examination and issues the certification. Atlantis prepares candidates; it certifies no one. To scope a course for yourself or your team, request a CWI exam prep quote.

What the six-day CWI exam prep course is

The course is preparation for an examination that someone else writes, runs and scores. It follows the topic areas AWS publishes for each part and spends its time where candidates usually lose marks: reading welding symbols quickly, applying a procedure to a joint detail, measuring welds accurately, and finding the right table in a code book while the clock runs. Every practice question is written by Atlantis to the published topic list. None is a real AWS examination question, and Atlantis has no access to the examination or anyone's results.

Three things stay with the candidate. You must meet the AWS education and work-experience rules, pass the AWS vision test, and apply to AWS and pay its examination fees directly. AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed this course.

Who the course is for

  • Welders and fitters moving into inspection or QC who need the theory, symbols and code reading that production work never taught them.
  • QC inspectors and supervisors who already accept welds informally and now need the credential a customer or specification calls for.
  • NDT technicians, especially VT, MT and UT technicians certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, who want a personal certification for the welding side of the job.
  • Welding and manufacturing engineers whose role requires a CWI on staff.
  • Employers preparing several people at once for an audit, a bridge or pipeline contract, or a new in-house QC team.

Not sure you meet the experience rules? Check the eligibility table below first. Candidates short of the CWI requirement sometimes start with the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) credential, which has lower experience thresholds; a CAWI inspects alongside a CWI or Senior CWI who makes final acceptance. AWS describes the CAWI as valid for three years and not renewable.

The six-day course outline

The outline is the same whether you study online or your employer has the six days delivered at its facility. Online candidates follow it as a study plan at their own pace; on-site groups cover one block per day.

DayFocusMain topics
Day 1Fundamentals IWelding processes, terms and definitions (AWS A3.0), joint design, weld and welding symbols (AWS A2.4)
Day 2Fundamentals IIMetallurgy basics, mechanical and destructive testing, discontinuities and their causes, NDT methods, fabrication math, safety, inspector duties and ethics
Day 3Practical (Part B)Measuring and gauging, weld size and profile, visual acceptance against supplied specifications, procedure and qualification record exercises
Day 4Code application (Part C)Navigating the chosen code book, clause structure, tables, acceptance criteria, qualification requirements
Day 5Timed practice examsPractice papers for Parts A, B and C under time limits, with full review
Day 6Review and exam readinessWeak-area review, exam-day strategy, application and documents checklist

Day 1: Fundamentals I

Day one builds the vocabulary the week depends on: the arc welding processes candidates meet most (shielded metal arc, gas metal arc, flux cored arc, gas tungsten arc and submerged arc), oxyfuel welding and cutting, and what each does to heat input, penetration and typical defects. Terminology follows AWS A3.0, Standard Welding Terms and Definitions, because the exam uses AWS terms precisely; "throat" and "effective throat" are different answers. Joint design covers joint types, groove and fillet geometry, root opening, bevel angle, root face and backing. The afternoon is welding symbols under AWS A2.4: reference line, arrow side and other side, supplementary, contour and finish symbols, and the size, length and pitch dimensions for fillet, groove, plug and slot welds. Symbol reading is drilled until it is fast, because symbols appear in every part of the exam.

Day 2: Fundamentals II

Day two is metallurgy and testing. Metallurgy stays practical: hardenability, preheat and interpass temperature, the heat-affected zone, and where hydrogen cracking, lamellar tearing and hot cracking come from. Destructive testing covers tensile, guided bend, hardness, Charpy impact and macro-etch tests and what each proves in a qualification. Discontinuities are taught as cause and effect, linking porosity, slag, incomplete fusion, incomplete joint penetration, undercut, overlap, cracks and arc strikes to the conditions that produce them. The NDT block explains what visual, penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic and radiographic testing can and cannot find, so a CWI knows which method to request. The day closes with fabrication math (unit conversion, areas, weld metal volume and simple ratios), welding safety under ANSI Z49.1, and the duties and ethical obligations of a welding inspector.

Day 3: Practical preparation (Part B)

Day three prepares for the practical part. In the AWS examination the candidate works with tools, specimens and documents that AWS supplies and answers questions that depend on measuring correctly and on applying procedure and qualification records correctly. The course practises those skills directly: reading fillet weld gauges and a multipurpose bridge cam gauge, measuring leg size, convexity, concavity, reinforcement and undercut depth, checking misalignment, and comparing each measurement with the acceptance criteria in the documents you are handed. Procedure exercises check whether the conditions on a job fall inside what a WPS and its PQR qualify. When the six days are delivered on site, the group uses the employer's own gauges and real weld samples from the shop floor, which ties the practice to the joints those inspectors will actually accept. For background on how procedures and welder tests connect, see the WPS, PQR and WPQ guide.

Day 4: Code application (Part C)

Part C is open book, so the skill under test is finding and applying the right provision quickly. Day four works inside the code book each candidate has chosen, for example AWS D1.1 for structural steel or API 1104 for pipelines. Candidates learn where definitions, design provisions, prequalified joints, qualification, fabrication, inspection and acceptance tables sit, and how annexes relate to the main text. Exercises use realistic problems. Is this undercut acceptable for this type of loading? Does this welder's test plate qualify this position and thickness range? What minimum preheat does the table require for this steel and thickness? How you will access the code book on exam day is set by AWS, so check your confirmation materials before you spend hours tabbing a paper copy.

Day 5: Timed practice exams

Day five is examination conditions. Candidates sit timed practice papers for Fundamentals, the practical question set and their code book, then review every wrong answer and the reasoning behind it. Pacing matters as much as knowledge: Part A has 150 questions, and working every math item longhand runs the clock down. The scores show where the last day should go.

Day 6: Weak-area review and exam readiness

The last day returns to the topics each candidate missed on day five, then covers logistics: booking the computer-based parts at a Prometric center, what to bring, splitting time across a paper, and flagging questions to revisit. It ends with a documents checklist for the AWS application: education evidence, experience verification, the visual acuity record and the code book choice.

How the AWS CWI examination works

CWI certification is governed by AWS QC1, Specification for AWS Certification of Welding Inspectors. In November 2026 AWS listed the 2016 edition with its amendment, QC1:2016-AMD1, as the governing document, alongside AWS B5.1, the specification for the qualification of welding inspectors. The examination has three parts, and AWS requires a minimum score of 72% on each part. Candidates receive one consolidated score report.

  • Part A, Fundamentals: 150 questions. AWS lists the subject areas as destructive testing, fabrication math, safety, metallurgy, nondestructive testing, welding symbols, WPS and PQR, and welding fundamentals. It is a computer-based test taken at a Prometric exam center.
  • Part B, Practical: hands-on activities with equipment AWS provides, plus 46 questions. The activities center on applying procedure and qualification records and using inspection tools and methods. AWS runs Part B itself at its seminar and examination locations in the United States and abroad.
  • Part C, Code Application: an open-book test of roughly 50 to 65 questions on the code book the candidate selected, also computer-based at a Prometric center.

AWS states that Prometric operates more than 450 exam centers worldwide, over 100 of them in the United States. Part B may need travel, because it happens only where AWS holds a practical session. AWS sets the order of the parts and the window between the practical and the computer-based parts, and your AWS confirmation letter carries the eligibility code you need to book with Prometric. AWS does not give time limits on its main CWI page, so check the current exam reference guide and your confirmation materials for the time allowed per part.

Eligibility: education, experience and the vision test

AWS combines formal education with documented welding-related work experience: the more relevant education you have, the less experience it requires. The table follows the requirements AWS published on its CWI page in November 2026. AWS can change them, so confirm on aws.org before you apply.

EducationMinimum welding-related work experience
Bachelor's degree or higher in welding engineering or welding technology1 year
Associate degree or higher in welding or non-welding engineering technology, engineering or physical science2 years
Engineering or technical courses that apply toward a welding bachelor's degree3 years
Completed trade or vocational courses4 years
High school diploma or approved equivalent5 years
8th grade schooling9 years
Less than 8th grade12 years

The experience must be welding-based work that someone can verify. QC1 frames qualifying experience around work on welded products, such as design, production, construction, inspection or repair, and AWS decides what counts. List dates, employers, the codes you worked to and what you actually did.

Vision is assessed separately. The AWS Visual Acuity Record asks for near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without corrective lenses, plus a color perception test, performed by an ophthalmologist, optometrist, physician, registered nurse or certified physician assistant. AWS also limits how old that eye examination can be when you sit the exam, so time it with your booking. Wearing glasses for close work does not exclude you. Atlantis does not test vision and cannot vouch for anyone's experience; both go straight to AWS.

Applying to AWS, step by step

  1. Gather evidence: diplomas or transcripts, plus a record of welding-related jobs with dates, duties and someone who can verify each one.
  2. Have the vision examination done on the current AWS form, close enough to your exam date.
  3. Choose your Part C code book.
  4. Apply to AWS and pay the AWS fees. AWS publishes current examination and seminar fees on aws.org; for planning, use the CWI exam budget planner.
  5. Book the practical with AWS, then book Parts A and C with Prometric using the eligibility code in your confirmation letter.
  6. Prepare, leaving room for timed practice before the exam.

Choosing your code book for Part C

AWS lets each candidate choose the code for Part C, and the choice shapes the career that follows as much as the score. The options AWS listed in November 2026 were:

  • AWS D1.1, Structural Welding Code, Steel (2020 edition)
  • API 1104, Welding of Pipelines and Related Facilities (22nd edition)
  • AWS D1.2, Structural Welding Code, Aluminum (2014 edition)
  • AWS D1.5, Bridge Welding Code (2020 edition, including Clause 12)
  • AWS D15.1, Railroad Welding Specification for Cars and Locomotives (2019 edition)
  • AWS D17.1, Specification for Fusion Welding for Aerospace Applications (2024 edition)
  • ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section IX together with ASME B31.1 and B31.3
  • An ISO standards option

Examination editions often trail the newest one in print: AWS D1.1:2025 is published, yet the listing named the 2020 edition. Study the edition AWS names and confirm it in the exam reference guide. As a rough guide, structural fabricators and erectors choose D1.1, pipeline contractors and inspectors choose API 1104, steel bridge fabricators choose D1.5, and people in power and process piping or pressure equipment lean toward the ASME option. The course works in whichever book you pick. Background: AWS D1.1, D1.1 weld acceptance criteria, AWS D1.5 and API 1104.

Preparing for Part B, the practical

Part B rewards careful measurement and careful reading rather than shop instinct. Three habits help.

  • Measure, then decide. Read the gauge, write the number, then compare it with the requirement. Judging a fillet "about right" by eye loses marks.
  • Read the documents before the specimen. The procedure, qualification record and acceptance criteria you are handed define the answer; a weld that passes on your job may fail against them.
  • Know the tools cold. Fillet weld gauges, a multipurpose bridge cam gauge, an undercut gauge, a hi-lo gauge for misalignment, a steel rule, calipers and a magnifier all need to feel familiar.

Visual examination is the core of a welding inspector's work, and the practical tests it. For structured practice in visual technique beyond the exam, Atlantis also runs VT Level 1 and VT Level 2 training under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, where the employer certifies the technician afterward. The Practical NDT welding workshop simulator lets you rehearse inspection steps in a browser. See also visual testing, weld inspection services and the weld inspection methods guide.

Studying online or training as an employer group

Individuals: online study with instructor support

Individual candidates study online. You get a study plan built on the six-day outline, course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and you can send questions to an instructor as you work through them. There are no scheduled class times; you set the pace around your shifts. You can spread the six days of material over several weeks of evenings and weekends, then save the timed papers for the stretch just before your exam.

Employers: six days at your facility

Employers can have the six days delivered at their own facility for a group of their staff. On-site delivery uses your welds, your gauges and, where it fits, your code and your procedures, which makes Part B and Part C practice concrete. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually and must meet the eligibility and vision rules personally; an employer cannot sponsor anyone around them.

After you pass: renewal, recertification and where CWI leads

AWS describes the CWI certification as valid for nine years, with renewal applications due at the third and sixth years after activation. AWS has required a current visual acuity record on file before it releases a renewal, so keep your eye examination up to date. At nine years you recertify. AWS lists several routes, including retaking the Part B practical, completing 80 professional development hours, holding Certified Radiographic Interpreter status, an AWS nine-year course, or passing an endorsement examination before the ninth year. AWS allows a short grace period and charges administrative fees for late submissions, so diary the dates.

From there the paths branch:

  • Senior CWI (SCWI): the AWS step for inspectors who run inspection programs, with its own eligibility and examination; see the Senior CWI pathway.
  • Endorsements: AWS offers additional code endorsements, which widen the codes you are recognized on and can count toward recertification.
  • ASNT NDT certification: performing ultrasonic, magnetic particle or penetrant testing needs method training, experience and certification under the employer's written practice. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training; see NDT Level 2 training and ASNT certification explained.
  • API in-service inspection: many CWIs in refining move on to API 510, 570 or 653 certification, which API runs under its own rules. Atlantis does not train for API certifications; the API inspector guide explains how they work.

CWI, ASNT NDT Level II and API inspector certifications compared

Welders moving into inspection often ask which credential to chase. The three answer different questions, and plenty of inspectors hold more than one.

AWS CWIASNT NDT Level II (SNT-TC-1A)API 510, 570 or 653
Who certifiesAWS, after its examinationYour employer, under its written practiceAPI, after its examination
Who holds itThe individual; it moves with you between employersTied to the certifying employerThe individual
What it coversWelding inspection before, during and after welding, mainly visual examination and document review against a codePerforming and interpreting one NDT method, such as UT, MT, PT or VTIn-service inspection of pressure vessels (510), process piping (570) or aboveground storage tanks (653)
Typical settingsFabrication shops, structural steel, bridges, pipeline constructionInspection companies, plants, fabricatorsRefineries, chemical plants, terminals
RenewalNine-year cycle with renewals at years three and sixInterval set in the written practiceOn the API recertification cycle
Where Atlantis fitsSix-day exam-prep courseSNT-TC-1A-based training; the employer certifiesAtlantis does not train for these

Put simply, a CWI judges whether a weld meets its code, an NDT Level II performs a test that finds what the eye cannot, and an API inspector looks at equipment already in service. More: AWS CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II, welding inspector vs NDT technician and, for international projects, CWI vs CSWIP 3.1.

What six days can and cannot do

Six days of focused preparation can organize years of shop experience into exam-ready knowledge and make the clock feel familiar. It cannot create qualifying experience, change your eyesight, or replace careful measurement on real work; candidates new to reading codes should plan extra study. Atlantis does not promise a pass, does not see the examination and does not report scores; AWS sends results to candidates. For what published figures say about difficulty by part, read CWI results by exam part, and for requirements and career value, CWI requirements and career impact.

CWI exam prep in US cities

Who hires CWIs and which codes dominate differ by region. City pages: Houston, Baton Rouge, Tampa, Jacksonville, Chicago, Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, New York, Los Angeles, Seattle, Dallas, Tulsa and Detroit. For Atlantis NDT courses nationwide, see NDT training in the USA.

What to send for a quote

  • Whether the course is for you alone or for a group, and how many people.
  • Each candidate's education and welding-related experience in outline, so eligibility questions surface early rather than after study has started.
  • The Part C code book each candidate intends to choose.
  • For on-site delivery: the facility location, the gauges and weld samples available, and the weeks that suit production.
  • Whether candidates have already applied to AWS or booked a practical.

Send the details through the CWI exam prep enquiry form; we reply within one business day. For the wider training catalog, see NDT training and the free NDT practice tests.

faq.q: How long is the Atlantis CWI exam prep course?
faq.a: Six days. Individuals work through the six-day outline online at their own pace with instructor support for questions; employers can have the six days delivered at their own facility for a group of staff. See the full outline on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

faq.q: Does the course make me a Certified Welding Inspector?
faq.a: No. AWS administers the CWI examination and issues the certification. The course prepares you for the three parts of the exam; you still need to meet the AWS eligibility rules, pass its vision test, apply and pass each part.

faq.q: Are the practice questions taken from the real AWS exam?
faq.a: No. Every practice question is original, written by Atlantis to the topic areas AWS publishes. Atlantis has no access to the examination or its question bank.

faq.q: What are the three parts of the CWI exam?
faq.a: Part A, Fundamentals (150 questions on welding processes, metallurgy, testing, symbols, safety, math and procedures); Part B, Practical (hands-on activities with AWS-supplied equipment plus 46 questions); and Part C, Code Application (an open-book test of roughly 50 to 65 questions on the code you choose).

faq.q: What score is needed on each part?
faq.a: AWS lists a minimum score of 72% on each of the three parts, reported on one consolidated score report. Check aws.org for the current rule when you apply.

faq.q: Where are the CWI exam parts taken?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based tests at Prometric exam centers. AWS runs Part B, the practical, at its own seminar and examination locations, so it may need travel. Your AWS confirmation letter gives the eligibility code you need to book with Prometric.

faq.q: How much work experience do I need for the CWI exam?
faq.a: It depends on education. AWS lists five years of welding-related experience for a high school diploma, one year with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology, and up to twelve years with less than 8th grade schooling. The full table is on this page; confirm the current rules on aws.org.

faq.q: What vision test does AWS require?
faq.a: The AWS Visual Acuity Record asks for near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without corrective lenses, and a color perception test, done by a qualified eye-care or medical professional within the time window AWS sets before your exam.

faq.q: Which code book should I choose for Part C?
faq.a: Choose the code you work to. Structural fabricators usually pick AWS D1.1, pipeline people API 1104, steel bridge fabricators AWS D1.5, and power or process piping people the ASME option. Study the edition AWS lists, which can be older than the newest edition in print.

faq.q: How long does CWI certification last?
faq.a: AWS describes it as valid for nine years, with renewal applications at the third and sixth years and recertification at nine years by one of the routes AWS lists, such as the Part B practical or professional development hours.

faq.q: Can my company have the course run at our plant or shop?
faq.a: Yes. The six days can be delivered at your facility for a group of your staff, using your own gauges, weld samples and, where it fits, your code. Each person still applies to AWS individually. Request a quote.

faq.q: Is a CWI the same as an ASNT NDT Level II?
faq.a: No. A CWI is a personal AWS certification for welding inspection, mainly visual examination and document review. An ASNT NDT Level II under SNT-TC-1A is certified by the employer for one test method such as UT, MT, PT or VT. Atlantis trains for ASNT NDT methods as well; see NDT Level 2 training.
